sections.text: Prefer using variety of local seasonal foods, vegetables and fruits

sections.locator: Page 12 / Rest during pregnancy / final bullet
sections.text: Do not overexert yourself and delegate few tasks to others.
Take milk and dairy products like curd, buttermilk, paneer-these are rich in calcium, proteins and vitamins.
Cereals, whole grains and pulses are good sources of proteins.
Green leafy vegetables are a rich source of iron and folic acid.
For non-vegetarians, meat, egg, chicken or fish are good sources of proteins, vitamins and iron.
Paneer, milk and other milk products, combined grains, seeds, nuts, egg, meat, poultry, soya beans.
You and your baby should be seen by a health worker on the day of delivery, and on 3rd day, 7th day and 6 weeks after delivery.

sections.locator: Page 16 / postpartum rest bullet / day scope

sections.text: Take immediate medical help if any complication occurs in yourself or your baby.

sections.locator: Page 14 / pregnancy danger signals and immediate-help instruction
sections.text: If any complications occur- seek help immediately to preserve your health and life. DANGER SIGNALS DURING PREGNANCY. Generalised weakness, easy fatigability and breathlessness. Severe pain in abdomen. Bleeding per vaginum. Excessive swelling in legs. Fever. Convulsions.

sections.locator: Page 16 / immediate-help instruction and Contact FRU list
sections.text: Take immediate medical help if any complication occurs in yourself or your baby. Contact F R U. Excessive vaginal bleeding. Inability to control defecation/urine. Foul smelling vaginal discharge. Difficulty in breathing. Blurred vision and fits. Fever. Fainting.
